{{DISPLAYTITLE:Similarities to ''Dune''}}
{{Spoiler_page|''[https://www.goodreads.com/series/45935-dune Dune]'' and related works, such as the [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1160419/ Denis Villeneuve film adaptations]}}

==Introduction==

This page is intended to contain a comprehensive list of all commonalities between ''The Wheel of Time'' and Frank Herbert's ''{{Wlink|Dune}}'' series.

{{SimilaritiesDisclaimer}}

{{Quote|'''QUESTION''': I love all the similarities between Frank Herbert's Dune and WOT. Was this intended? If so, are you a fan of his?
'''ROBERT JORDAN''': No, there was no intention to make any similarities between Dune and my writings. And I am certainly a big fan of the original Dune novel. Although I doubt if I've read it since it first came out!|[[Source:MSN - eFriends Interviews Robert Jordan, 11 November 1998|MSN eFriends Interview]]{{ref/tidb|96|5}}}}

==Story==
*The protagonist is forced to flee when his home and father are attacked.
*Eventually, the protagonist seeks out a desert warrior people and recruits them to his own purposes.[[File:Jeremy Saliba aiel take 2.jpg|thumb|Aiel]]
**Part of this recruitment involves undergoing a highly dangerous ritual that reveals the desert people's history.
*The protagonist gains a young female companion who teaches him the desert people's ways and ultimately becomes his lover. At one point, the protagonist unknowingly takes action that incidentally has courtship implications in the desert culture.
*With the desert warriors as his principle fighting force, the protagonist conquers much of the civilization previously dominated by a unifying empire. In particular, he confronts the rulers of the old empire and reaches a fragile arrangement with them.
*[[Rand]] battles [[Ishamael]] with the sword similar to how {{Wlink|dune|Paul}} battles {{Wlink|dune|Feyd-Rautha}} with knives.

==Characters and creatures==
*[[Rand al'Thor]] and {{Wlink|dune|Paul Atreides}}[[File:Rand dragon.jpg|thumb|Rand al'Thor]]
**Both are messiah figures in our distant future.
***Rand differs from standard messiah figures in that he is dreaded and feared, to the extent that he is sometimes conflated with [[Dark One|Shai'tan]].{{ref/book|1|3}}
***Paul differs from standard fantasy messiah figures in that he is a false messiah, but he is also - in a manner of speaking - a true messiah.
***Both are overall "good" protagonists with pronounced dark sides.
**Multiple concurrent female romantic/marriage relationships.
**Master fighters - Rand with the sword and Paul with knives and hand-to-hand combat.
**Rand/Paul participate in a deadly Aiel/Fremen ritual that reveals the Aiel/Fremen past to Rand/Paul and survive.
{{Quote|“The [[Dragon]]!” someone moaned. “The [[Dark One]]’s loose in [[Ghealdan]]!”
“Not the Dark One,” [[Haral Luhhan]] growled. “The Dragon’s not the Dark One. And this is a false Dragon, anyway.”|{{1|3}}{{ref/book|1|3}}}}
*[[Aviendha]] and {{Wlink|dune|Chani}}
**Both come from the desert warrior race the protagonist recruits to his cause.
**Both initially distrust the protagonist and yet are given the task of instructing him in their culture.
**Both protagonists unintentionally mimic one of their courting customs.
**Both are the first lover of the protagonist to engage in intercourse with him.
**Both bear children to the protagonist (though Aviendha's children are born after the series ends).
**Both have a princess "rival" that is not truly a rival for the protagonist's affections.
*[[Elayne Trakand]] and {{Wlink|dune|Irulan|Irulan}}
**Princesses of arguably the strongest state in the known world at the start of the series.
**Both have very unusual interruptions to their ascension to the throne.
***Elayne engages in an Andoran [[Succession Wars|Succession crisis]] despite being [[Daughter-Heir]].
***Irulan's father is usurped by Paul.
**Both of their respective kingdoms are apparently conquered by the protagonist (though this is not actually true in Elayne/[[Andor]]'s case).
**Both of their respective kingdoms' rulers sit on a [[Lion Throne]].
*[[Elayne Trakand]]'s male-female twin children remind one of {{Wlink|dune|Chani}}'s children {{Wlink|dune|Leto II}} and his older twin sister {{Wlink|dune|Ghanima}}.
*[[Rhuarc]] and {{Wlink|dune|Stilgar|Stilgar}}
**Chiefs of their respective subsets of the [[Aiel]]/{{Wlink|dune|Fremen}}.
**Among the first of their people to meet the protagonist.
**One of the first of their people to acknowledge the protagonist as their prophesied [[Car'a'carn]]/{{Wlink|dune|Lisan al Gaib}}
**Is consistently one of the most reliable if not the most reliable lieutenant and general of the protagonist.
*[[Moiraine Damodred]] and Jessica are Aes Sedai/Bene Gesserit who join the Wise Ones / Reverend Mothers (to an extent) at least partially to stay close to Rand/Paul and takes part in their supernatural rituals.

==Locations==
*Notwithstanding {{Wlink|dune|Arrakis}} being a sandy desert and the [[Aiel Waste]] being badlands, both are water-scarce deserts where the "chosen one" protagonist sojourns to garner support among the natives.[[File:World Aiel Waste.png|thumb|The Aiel Waste]]

==Magic and artifacts==
*Men with [[Aes Sedai]]/{{Wlink|dune|Bene Gesserit}} abilities are generally prohibited prior to the birth of the protagonist. The protagonist defies this and sets about creating more such men, figuratively and deliberately in [[Rand]]'s case and literally and incidentally in Paul's case.
*[[Sa'angreal]], especially those that - like [[Callandor]] - take the form of conventional weapons, were potentially going to be called ''cris''.{{ref/rignotes|45|2|3|Background Notes on The Wheel of Time}}{{ref/rignotes|45|2|2-3|Wheel of Time: Notes 13a}} The name and concept were derived from the {{Wiki|Kris|Javanese kris knife}}.{{ref/book|origins|Turns}} The {{Wlink|dune|Fremen}} ''{{Wlink|dune|crysknife}}'' has obvious etymological similarities.[[File:Javanese kris knife Tropen Museum Collection MET schede TMnr A-1448.jpg|thumb|Javanese kris knife]][[File:Crysknife by Matt Howarth.webp|thumb|Fremen crysknife]]

==Peoples and Institutions==
*The [[Aes Sedai]] of the [[Third Age]] and the {{Wlink|dune|Bene Gesserit}} are very, very old female-only institutions that wield supernatural powers and attempt to control the main civilization through political machinations.
*The [[Aiel]] and {{Wlink|dune|Fremen}} are both proud warrior races used as a tool by the protagonist for gaining political power in the story's main civilization with the ultimate goal being the salvation of humanity.
**Both are characterized by extreme violence and largely revolve around the procurement and distribution of water.
**Both are led in part by semi-mystic women with supernatural powers who are the local counterparts to the main institution of female "magic" users ([[Wise One|Wise Ones]]/Reverend Mothers). They are in some sense an offshoot of the main institution (Age of Legends Aes Sedai / Bene Gesserit).
*[[Artur Hawkwing's Empire]] and the [[Seanchan]] Empire (inasmuch as it is a successor state to Hawkwing's empire) are similar to {{Wlink|dune|Corrino Empire|The Corrino Empire}}.
